newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Deals worth $1-bln crown Kohl's Manila trip.
newsitem.headline: Deals worth $1-bln crown Kohl's Manila trip.

text.p: Germany and the Philippines signed business deals worth nearly $1 billion on Tuesday, crowning the first day of German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's three-day visit to the Pacific country.

"The signing of the agreements has put out a marker on the road toward further intensification of our cooperation," the first German head of government to visit the Philippines told a news conference after talks with President Fidel Ramos.

The biggest deal signed by businessmen of the two countries was an agreement by Siemens AG with the Philippines' First Gas Holdings Corp to build a gas-fired, 990-megawatt power plant near Manila. The project is worth $650 million.
First Gas is a joint venture of British Gas and First Philippine Holdings Corp
Kohl, who arrived from Indonesia, is on the second leg of an Asian tour that will take him to Japan on Wednesday.
His trip coincided with calls from Germany's opposition Social Democrats for him to cut his trip to answer questions in parliament on the budget. Kohl's office said he would not do so.
But a cabinet minister in Kohl's party told journalists six deputies from Kohl's coalition would break off from the Asian tour and rush back to Bonn for the debate on Wednesday.
Kohl brushed aside a German reporter's question on the issue at a news conference.
"I don't think I am under any duress to explain anything and I don't intend to speak about domestic issues in a press conference in a foreign country," he said through an interpreter.
Unlike in Indonesia, there was no East Timor to shadow his visit to Manila.
He said he and Ramos did not discuss the issue. "It's as simple as that," he said.
Kohl had failed to meet East Timor Catholic bishop and Nobel Peace laureate Carlos Belo in his trip to Indonesia despite arrangements made for such a meeting.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move never recognised by the United Nations.

Ramos himself has come under fire at home after he barred the visit of East Timorese resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta during next month's summit of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
Kohl said APEC "should champion the cause of free trade".
"When we say in Europe that we do not want to set up a 'fortress Europe', then obviously we would like to see the same kind of development...in other parts of the world," he said.
Kohl indicated it was inevitable for Germany to play a political as well as an economic role in Asia.
"Actually we're doing that now already," he said, adding no country could separate economics and politics in its policies.
"I believe that a policy that is only oriented towards the political field is bound to fail because what would be behind that would be a pure spirit of materialism," he said.

Other deals signed during Kohl's first day was a $266 million joint venture agreement Deutsche Telekom and Asiacom cellular phone subisidiary IslaCom and a $33 million financial cooperation agrement for port construction and navigational aids for Philippine inter-island shipping.
